o1.biggest_strength: It catches the big launch risk: hotkey and extension migration must be proven before launch, with support and staged rollout built around it.
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel table is confusing because it ranks extension authors above X while showing X retained more users, and it leaves several launch-copy placeholders to fill.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the channel ranking logic, add owners to every timeline item, and replace placeholders with final-ready copy or clear fill rules.

o2.biggest_strength: It turns the data into a practical launch sequence with owners, dates, gates, support targets, tracking, and a clear plan B.
o2.biggest_mistake: It says channels are ranked by users who stay but actually mixes retention rate, absolute retained users, and strategic potential, and it gives Product Hunt launch-day space despite its weak retention.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Separate absolute retained-user ranking from strategic channel priority, and move Product Hunt to a lower-effort follow-up day.

reason: Output 2 is the one I could hand to the team fastest: it has owners, done-when criteria, targets, and a plan B while staying tight. Output 1 is also strong, but it is a little less operational and has more confusing ranking and placeholder work left.
